claims.text: The initial magnetic high-entropy alloy is homogeneous, single-phase, and has moderate coercivity.
Intermediate-temperature post-synthesis aging can induce L12-type precipitates in an initially homogeneous magnetic high-entropy alloy.
Optimized aging will produce a uniform distribution of nanoscale L12-type precipitates.
Increasing the volume fraction of an L12 phase can be accompanied by increased lattice misfit and slightly increased coercivity in magnetic HEAs.
Nanoscale L12 precipitates introduce internal lattice misfit.
Nanoscale L12 precipitates introduce additional high-angle boundaries.
The L12 precipitates act as effective domain-wall pinning centers.
Aging-induced nanoscale L12 precipitation will increase coercive field relative to an unaged, otherwise matched alloy.
The coercivity increase will be statistically significant.
Coercivity enhancement will occur only within an optimized aging-temperature and aging-time window that yields nanoscale precipitates.
Overly severe heat treatment may coarsen the precipitates and thereby prevent an increase in coercivity.
Overly mild heat treatment may produce no precipitation and therefore no increase in coercivity.
The proposed effect should hold at moderate measurement temperatures where the precipitate-containing microstructure remains stable.
Matched aged and unaged samples can be compared using microscopy and magnetic hysteresis measurements.
Failure to observe a statistically significant coercivity increase after confirming the targeted precipitates would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to form the targeted precipitates would itself falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The design says the treatment will retain a homogeneous alloy composition while also producing precipitates. If homogeneous refers to local composition or a single phase, precipitation necessarily creates compositional or structural heterogeneity; this would be consistent only if 'homogeneous' means unchanged overall nominal composition.
